description:
Goal
Remove telemetry ownership from semantic World so World is an owned, lifetime-free authority that synchronous handlers can borrow directly.

Current state
World<'a> stores &'a dyn Telemetry. This couples every semantic API to observer lifetime, prevents World from satisfying Any, encourages emit sites to flatten World state into metadata, and prevents a statically owned NullTelemetry specialization at the Compiler2 boundary.

Strategy
- Make World contain semantic state only.
- Make Compiler2<T> own World and a telemetry implementation T separately.
- Introduce a short-lived execution/job context that reborrows &mut World and &T for operations requiring both.
- Keep state mutations in World; return or expose the already-existing decision result. After the mutable borrow ends, the context lazily emits an immutable &World plus raw decision-local references.
- Do not introduce Rc into World, global telemetry, unsafe lifetime erasure, a World facade duplicating state, or compatibility forwarding methods.

TDD
First add compile-time/type tests showing World has no lifetime or telemetry field and can be borrowed as an opaque event-scoped value. Preserve existing semantic behavior and telemetry event ordering during this ownership-only move.

Acceptance
- World is lifetime-free and telemetry-free.
- Compiler2 can be instantiated with owned NullTelemetry or configured telemetry.
- Jobs receive telemetry only through the short-lived execution context.
- Existing tests remain green before payload/API migration.
- Docs describe observer ownership; clippy passes.

comments.text: SPIKE PROOF: target is viable; no prototype commit because a partial migration would knowingly not compile or would drop observations. World becomes lifetime-free semantic state; Compiler2<T: Telemetry> owns World+T; short-lived ExecutionContext holds split &mut World and &dyn Telemetry. Explicit World lifetime surface is 26 production files; 213 World::new(&tel) and 566 Compiler2::new(&tel) call sites. Move drive/complete_job/warning emission to Context; jobs::run takes Context; pure helpers remain World; product producers split world/tel; dump emitters take (&World, tel); lowerers take Context only if they emit. Critical borrow rule: destructure Context fields before opening spans/ProductDriver; end mutable store borrows before emitting immutable &World. Do not Deref Context to World, add a forwarding facade, unsafe erase lifetimes, or store Rc telemetry in World. Atomicity confirmed: owning World+telemetry while World borrows telemetry is self-referential, and splitting into independently green commits would require forbidden scaffolding. Spike baseline checks: cargo check --lib; world 19/19; compiler2 front door 12/12; product_drive 11/11; telemetry_dump 4/4 (2 ignored).

title: Remove telemetry ownership and lifetime from World
